standard_prerequisites.name: Pattern containment and avoidance
standard_prerequisites.statement: A matching m_2 contains m_1 when an order-preserving choice of vertices carries the chords and unmatched vertices of m_1 to those of m_2, and a set of matchings avoids m_1 when none of its members contains it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the notion appearing in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary Knuth transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: Knuth equivalence is generated by a local rewriting of three consecutive chords of a matching.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof only has to check one such transformation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Short-chord-free pattern
standard_prerequisites.statement: The pattern m is assumed to have no short chord, so no chord of m joins two consecutive vertices.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the case distinction in the proof exhaustive.

core_obligations: Reduce to a single elementary Knuth transformation applied to a matching of the avoiding set, since a Knuth equivalence is a sequence of such transformations (source line 1305).
Assume the original matching contains the pattern m and exhibit a choice of vertices witnessing that the transformed matching contains m as well (source line 1305).

Distinguish the two cases according to whether the index shifted by the transformation belongs to the witnessing set, and build the new witness accordingly, which is where the absence of short chords in m is used (source line 1306).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce Knuth equivalence to one elementary transformation and set up the witness.
Rebuild the witness set in the two possible cases and conclude that the pattern is still contained.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1300-1303: for a short-chord-free matching m, the set of matchings of given size and number of unmatched vertices that avoid m is closed under Knuth equivalence. The proof (source lines 1304-1307) reduces to a single elementary Knuth transformation, then takes a witness for the containment of m in the original matching and has to rebuild it for the transformed matching; the reconstruction splits into two cases according to whether the vertex moved by the transformation is part of the witness, and both cases are only non-degenerate because the pattern has no short chord. The statement records the closure property and neither the reduction nor the case analysis.
